text:
alex: Quick check on embeddings API behavior before we merge the client change. Two things: truncation semantics and max batch size.

maya: tl;dr — current server truncates by bytes at UTF-8 boundary which has caused weird token splits. we talked about switching to token-based truncation (model tokenizer) — is that live? :thinking_face: 

jonah: Not live yet. infra PR open but blocked on compatibility tests. Main risk: some customers depend on exact returned vector dims/ordering for batching.

alex: Specific questions: 1) If input is a list of strings, and some are over limit, do we drop, error, or truncate? 2) What is the hard max inputs per request? 3) Is output vector order guaranteed to match input order even with truncation?

maya: Answers from spec side: 1) We should TRUNCATE each over-limit string (not drop). 2) Hard max is 512 items per request for hosted; Dedicated can be configured but API should return 413 with hint header when exceeded. 3) Yes order must be preserved — that's a backward-compat guarantee.

jonah: Implementation notes: we'll move truncation to token-level using the serving tokenizer for the selected model. For mixed-model rollouts there will be a translation layer that applies model-specific token budgets.

alex: Good. What about empty strings and nulls? Some clients send ["", null, "text"]. Behavior today?

maya: Current behavior: empty string -> returns zero-vector? actually returns embedding for empty input (non-zero) because model treats empty as context-less request. null currently rejected with 400. Proposal: accept empty string and return normal embedding; keep rejecting null and return clear error message.

eva: +1 to rejecting null. we should add a client-side linting note in the SDKs to convert null->"" intentionally if people want a placeholder.

alex: Back-compat: older models returned 1536-d floats; newer ones 1024-d. Are we adding a response field to make this explicit?

jonah: Yes — adding response metadata: "vector_dim": 1024 (or 1536) and "model": "embed-model-v2". Also returning "truncated": [false,true,false] aligning with inputs so callers can surface warnings.

alex: Can you paste the proposed sample response shape for clients?

jonah: Sure:

```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "embed-model-v2",
  "inputs": ["short text", "a very long text...", "another"]
}

200 OK
{
  "model": "embed-model-v2",
  "vector_dim": 1024,
  "data": [
    { "embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ...], "input_index": 0, "truncated": false },
    { "embedding": [0.12, 0.03, ...], "input_index": 1, "truncated": true },
    { "embedding": [0.09, -0.01, ...], "input_index": 2, "truncated": false }
  ]
}
```

maya: Note: we include input_index for absolute safety (keeps order clear even if we someday parallelize). Also we will include header X-Inputs-Limit: 512 on 413 responses.

sanjay: infra question — when truncation happens we should emit metrics: embedding.truncated_count, embedding.truncation_by_model, and expose a sample warning in logs. ok to add?

jonah: yes, add metrics. also attach a small sample text hash in logs to help debug without storing PII.

alex: Action items: 
- jonah: finish token-based truncation patch and add "vector_dim" and "truncated" flags (due EOD Fri)
- maya: update API spec and SDK linting note (due Tue)
- sanjay: add metrics + X-Inputs-Limit header behavior (due EOD Thu)

maya: I'll also add a short note to /docs/embeddings about null vs empty behavior and example migration snippet for clients.

alex: Perfect. If no objections, i'll merge the client change once jonah's patch is in staging. :thumbsup: 

infra-bot: deploy scheduled to staging at 2026-03-18T03:00:00Z — job id deploy-99321 :rocket: 

alex: thanks, everyone. ping me if you hit compatibility edgecases. :eyes:
